floor_rows.evidence: CBO corrected direction: average MA and FFS premiums lower than current law
CBO: MA enrollees would pay more out of pocket on average
CBO: MA enrollees would receive fewer supplemental benefits
MedPAC baseline is robust at 39 plans and eight organizations on average; policy effect is not quantified
MedPAC reports high satisfaction but finds the quality-bonus and star-rating systems inadequate for expected quality and access comparison
Age, disability, dual eligibility, ESRD, income, race and ethnicity, geography, and rural effects are not scored for this option
Existing FFS hospital-margin floor does not measure MA network or negotiated-payment effects
Plan bid response, exits, network changes, implementation cost, and transition mitigation are not quantified

mitigation_requirements: cap or offset beneficiary out-of-pocket increases by income and health status
protect high-value supplemental benefits for vulnerable enrollees
measure county and plan exits, network adequacy, and rural effects
replace or supplement the quality-bonus evidence with valid quality and access measures
quantify plan bid response, implementation cost, and transition behavior
rescore the mitigated instrument against the February 2026 current-law baseline

candidate_decision.next_candidate_strategy: target excess-payment drivers and add beneficiary mitigation rather than apply an unmitigated uniform benchmark cut

public_warning: The uniform 10 percent benchmark candidate fails the current no-regression screen because CBO expects higher average out-of-pocket costs and fewer supplemental benefits, while five other required floors remain unquantified. The $489 billion official score and $497.044 billion proxy remain excluded from the spending package.
